children: was downgraded to Equal Weight from Overweight at Wells Fargo on Monday, though the firm kept its $194 price target.

“We don't foresee either F4Q print, or Investor Day as [positive] catalysts,” analyst Jason Kupferberg wrote in a note to clients. “Ongoing [Middle East] headwinds could make F27 [constant currency] organic growth acceleration challenging. Valuation [and] buyback may limit downside while AI debates continue.”

Delving deeper, Kupferberg said the upcoming investor day (held on Oct. 14) is likely to offer some examples of how artificial intelligence is benefiting Accenture, but any “specific multi-year financial targets seem less likely relative to a qualitative financial framework.” There's also likely to be a focus on the company's M&A strategy, given that Accenture has made some “large deals” recently, Kupferberg added.

“We believe AI can ultimately be a tailwind for ACN, but size may be [a near-term] disadvantage,” Kupferberg explained. “We believe ingredients exist for ACN to be an AI beneficiary (strong C-level relationships, domain/tech expertise, ability to navigate prior paradigm shifts); but it may take time for ACN to see net benefits to top-line growth. ACN's size (~800,000 employees) may also complicate the AI transition, and until organic revs accelerate materially, it may be challenging to convince the Street that ACN is an AI winner.”

title: Accenture downgraded to Equal Weight at Wells Fargo
